# Assess privacy impact before a processing change

[Overview](#overview) · [Before you start](#before-you-start) · [Steps](#steps-at-a-glance)

## Overview

Before a new or materially changed use of personal data that may carry elevated privacy risk. A reviewed assessment with mitigation owners, residual-risk approval and a recorded launch decision.

Start with the applicability facts and evidence listed in the first step. Resolve missing facts before authorizing the affected work. Completion requires the documented outcome, including tracked exceptions; starting an application or recording a task is not evidence of completion.

> This is an operational coordination guide. Confirm the applicable company facts, contracts and jurisdictions before acting. Qualified advisers own legal, tax, safety or regulatory determinations and any required professional work. The cited authorities describe their named jurisdictions or frameworks; their rules are not asserted for other countries. External actions require approval for the specific action.

> Editorial status: operational draft. Source pages checked on 2026-10-29. No case-specific legal review, professional assurance or completed execution is claimed.

## Step details

<a id="step-1"></a>

### 1. Describe the processing and affected people

agent-runnable


Document the purpose, data categories, people, recipients, systems and intended decisions. Map collection through deletion and identify vulnerable groups, monitoring or sensitive information for specialist review.

- Sources: [GOV.UK data protection and your business](https://www.gov.uk/data-protection-your-business) · [European Commission international data protection](https://commission.europa.eu/law/law-topic/data-protection/international-dimension-data-protection_en)

<a id="step-2"></a>

### 2. Determine the assessment and consultation requirements

human · human approval required


The privacy lead and qualified advisers decide which local assessments, reviews or consultations apply. Record the criteria and applicable scope without treating a global checklist as legal approval.

- Sources: [GOV.UK data protection and your business](https://www.gov.uk/data-protection-your-business) · [European Commission international data protection](https://commission.europa.eu/law/law-topic/data-protection/international-dimension-data-protection_en)

<a id="step-3"></a>

### 3. Evaluate necessity, alternatives and risks

agent-runnable


Describe less intrusive ways to meet the purpose and assess misuse, access, accuracy, security and downstream effects. Support proposed safeguards with evidence and name the owners of unresolved questions.

- Sources: [GOV.UK data protection and your business](https://www.gov.uk/data-protection-your-business) · [European Commission international data protection](https://commission.europa.eu/law/law-topic/data-protection/international-dimension-data-protection_en)

<a id="step-4"></a>

### 4. Approve mitigations and residual risk

human · human approval required


Accountable owners review the assessment and required advice before authorizing the defined use. Keep launch paused for unresolved mandatory approvals or unacceptable risks and record the exact conditions of acceptance.

- Sources: [GOV.UK data protection and your business](https://www.gov.uk/data-protection-your-business) · [European Commission international data protection](https://commission.europa.eu/law/law-topic/data-protection/international-dimension-data-protection_en)

<a id="step-5"></a>

### 5. Verify implementation and reassessment triggers

agent-runnable


Check that approved controls, notices and contracts match the deployed system. Calendar review and reopen the assessment when data, purposes, vendors, technology or affected populations materially change.

- Verify: A reviewed assessment with mitigation owners, residual-risk approval and a recorded launch decision.
- Sources: [GOV.UK data protection and your business](https://www.gov.uk/data-protection-your-business) · [European Commission international data protection](https://commission.europa.eu/law/law-topic/data-protection/international-dimension-data-protection_en)
